references.text: God commanded Israel to attack the Midianites because of their seduction at Peor, which led to sin and plague among the people of Israel.
The background for the vengeance against the Midianites: The people of Israel sinned with Moabite and Midianite women and worshiped Baal-Peor.
God told Moses that he would be gathered to his people after seeing the promised land; this same expression is used here regarding his death.
The expression 'gathered to his people' is also used concerning Abraham's death, a Hebrew euphemism for dying.
Moses' death is described with the same expression 'gathered to his people' as Aaron was gathered.
Aaron was 'gathered to his people' on Mount Hor, the same expression used regarding Moses' upcoming death.
The Midianite kings who were killed in this act of vengeance are mentioned as an example of God's judgment.
Isaiah refers to the victory over Midian as an example of God's mighty salvation.
